To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the measured excitation energies of the hot nuclei formed in these collisions are in good agreement with predictions based on the assumption that the hot nuclei formed are in thermal equilibrium, (ii) the measured exciter energies and multiplicities of emitted particles are in good agreement, within experimental uncertainties, with those predicted by a statistical model based on the assumption of thermal equilibrium, (iii) there is no evidence for the production, in these collisions, of hot nuclei that are out of thermal equilibrium,

the hot nuclei produced in the reactions studied here have decay patterns that are independent of the entrance channel and that these decay patterns are consistent with the assumption of thermal equilibration.

(i) the hot nuclei produced in the reactions studied here have excitation energies in the range of about 2 to 4 MeV/nucleons and (ii) their decay is dominated by the emission of a few light charged particles, with a small fraction of the total kinetic energy being carried by the lightest emitted particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of nuclear reactions at high excitation energies.
the study of the properties of hot nuclei produced in the near-Fermi energy heavy-ion reactions.
the production, identification, and characterization of hot nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are compatible with a picture of a hot nucleus with a Fermi energy distribution and an equilibrated temperature.
, in heavy-ion collisions, equilibration of the hot composite system is attained at the Fermi energy.

the hot nuclei produced in these reactions are very close to thermal equilibrium, and that the observed deviations from equilibrium behavior are due to the finite size of the system, which is of the order of 10 nucleons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hot nuclei produced in these heavy-ion collisions are equilibrated in the time scale of 0.5 x 10(-20) s.
the observed decay patterns for hot nuclei produced with different entrance channels are consistent with the production of hot equilibrated nuclei with a temperature of 5 to 7 MeV.
the composite systems produced in the reactions are in a state of thermal and chemical equilibrium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hot nuclei produced in these collisions are in a state that is very near equilibrium.
, in spite of the large number of degrees of freedom, the system is able to thermalize in a time scale much smaller than the expansion time scale.
the hot nuclei are produced in a state of approximate equilibrium.
